newsitem.title: GERMANY: German industry orders jump 3.3 pct in April.
newsitem.headline: German industry orders jump 3.3 pct in April.

text.p: German industrial orders grew 3.3 percent in April from the preceding month, the Economics Ministry said, an unusually strong gain compared with a 0.9 percent rise in March.
Orders were up 6.2 percent from the year-earlier month, after a 5.5 percent annual gain in March.
The ministry said orders were again boosted by some large contracts, primarily from outside Germany. Overall domestic orders were up 3.1 percent, while foreign orders rose 3.6 percent.

Foreign orders for German capital goods were up 5.0 percent, while similar orders for German consumer goods rose 7.0 percent. But even domestic consumer goods showed a surprisingly strong 6.2 percent rise after declining 1.1 percent in March.
West German orders were up 3.3 percent month-on-month and 5.3 percent year-on-year, while east German orders rose 4.0 percent and 21.1 percent, respectively.

The data painted a much brighter picture of the economy than April industrial production data released on Wednesday, which showed a 1.3 percent month-on-month decline, and only a 1.3 percent rise from the year-earlier month.
